newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK RESTORES FIXING CALCULATION METHOD.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK RESTORES FIXING CALCULATION METHOD.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) met a recommendation by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), saying it would restore its practice of calculating a daily lev/dollar fixing irrespective of daily traded volumes.

"From March 18 the daily calculation of foreign currency fixings will be based on daily interbank volumes of foreign exchange bought and sold. January amendments (concerning the volumes) are being scrapped," a BNB statement said.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) recommended that the BNB should return to calculating the fixings irrespective of traded volumes before a new $650 million accord with the IMF was approved by the IMF board, possibly in the second week of April.

Today's BNB decision was linked to a rise of interbank traded volumes, the lack of wide gyrations in the lev/dollar exchange rate and the narrower bid/ask spread for the dollar against the lev in March, the statement said.
In January the BNB decided to change its daily foreign currency fixings only if traded interbank volumes for the day were higher than $10 million sold and $10 million bought, respectively.
But the change resulted in a large disparity between the fixings and the actual market exchange rates.

The BNB then further amended the method, saying if daily traded volumes for three consecutive days were below $10 million bought and $10 million sold, it would calculate the lev/dollar fix on the basis of the total turnover for those days. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 8569
